paragraphs: More people in Ireland are homeless. New figures came out on Friday. They were late because some workers were on strike.
In September, 18,065 people lived in emergency accommodation. That is 180 more than in August.
This number includes 5,897 children. They live in 2,821 families. There are also 7,379 adults with no children.
Most of the adults are men. About half of the adults are Irish. Many are between 25 and 44 years old.
A charity leader said the figures are very sad. Another group said more than 5,000 women are now in emergency accommodation. The groups want the Government to do more.
The numbers do not count everyone. For example, people who sleep on the street are not in them.

另一個團體說，現在有超過5,000名女性住在緊急安置住所。

paragraphs: The number of homeless people in Ireland has gone up again. The Department of Housing published the September figures on Friday evening. They were supposed to come out on 30 October, but they were late because of industrial action by workers.

In September, 18,065 people were living in emergency accommodation. This was 180 more than in August. Among them were 5,897 children in 2,821 families. There were also 7,379 single adults who did not have children with them.

The figures also show who is homeless. More than 58% of the adults were men, and more than half of the adults were between 25 and 44 years old. Half of the adults were Irish citizens. Another 31.4% came from countries outside the European Economic Area, and 18.6% came from the European Economic Area or the UK.
Dublin has the biggest problem. In one week in late September, more than 8,300 adults stayed in emergency accommodation run by local councils in the city. Of these, 4,940 were single adults.

Charities are worried. Ber Grogan, who leads the Simon Communities of Ireland, said the figures were "astoundingly depressing". She pointed out that there were 47 more children in emergency accommodation than in the month before. The Dublin Simon Community said it was very worried because, for the second month in a row, more than 5,000 adult women were in emergency accommodation. It said the numbers were 4.5% higher than a year ago, and it asked the Government to take action.

The real number may be even higher. The official figures do not include people who sleep on the streets, people who stay on friends' sofas, or people in domestic violence refuges. They also leave out people in direct provision, the housing system for people seeking asylum, who cannot find a home.

paragraphs: Homelessness in Ireland has risen once again, according to figures published by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage on Friday evening. The September data had been due on 30 October but was delayed by industrial action.

A total of 18,065 people were in emergency accommodation during September, an increase of 180 on August. The figure included 5,897 children belonging to 2,821 families, as well as 7,379 single adults without dependent children.

The data also offers a profile of homeless adults. Men made up more than 58% of the total, and the largest age group was 25 to 44, accounting for over 51%. Half of adults held Irish citizenship, 31.4% were from outside the European Economic Area and 18.6% were from the EEA or the UK.

The pressure is most intense in Dublin. In the week from 21 to 27 September, more than 8,300 adults relied on emergency accommodation provided by local authorities in the capital, 4,940 of whom were single.

Ber Grogan, executive director of Simon Communities of Ireland, described the figures as "astoundingly depressing", noting that 47 more children were in emergency accommodation than a month earlier. Dublin Simon Community expressed deep concern that the number of adult women in emergency accommodation had passed 5,000 for the second consecutive month. It highlighted a 4.5% rise compared with the same time last year and urged the Government to act.

Campaigners stress that the official count does not capture the full scale of the crisis. It excludes people sleeping rough, those couch-surfing with friends or relatives, people in domestic violence refuges, and residents of direct provision centres who are unable to secure housing.

都柏林西蒙社區對成年女性住在緊急安置住所的人數連續第二個月超過5,000人深表關切。

paragraphs: Ireland's homelessness figures have climbed yet again, with the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage releasing its September statistics on Friday evening. Their publication, originally scheduled for 30 October, had been postponed owing to industrial action.

The data shows that 18,065 people were living in emergency accommodation in September, 180 more than in August. Among them were 5,897 children from 2,821 families, alongside 7,379 single adults with no dependants.

A breakdown of the adult population reveals a striking pattern. Men accounted for upwards of 58%, while those aged 25 to 44 constituted the largest cohort, at more than 51%. Half held Irish citizenship, 31.4% were nationals of countries beyond the European Economic Area, and the remaining 18.6% came from the EEA or the UK.
Dublin remains the epicentre of the crisis. During the week of 21 to 27 September, upwards of 8,300 adults were housed in local-authority emergency accommodation in the capital, 4,940 of them single.

Advocacy groups reacted with dismay. Ber Grogan, executive director of Simon Communities of Ireland, branded the figures "astoundingly depressing", pointing out that 47 additional children had entered emergency accommodation within a single month. Dublin Simon Community voiced profound concern that, for the second month running, more than 5,000 adult women were in emergency accommodation, and drew attention to a 4.5% year-on-year increase, calling on the Government to intervene.

Moreover, the official tally offers only a partial picture. It omits rough sleepers, people couch-surfing, those in domestic violence refuges and residents of direct provision who are unable to find housing, so the true extent of homelessness is likely to be greater still.

這份數據原定於10月30日公布，但因勞資行動而延期。
數據顯示，九月有18,065人住在緊急安置住所，比八月多180人。
其中包括來自2,821個家庭的5,897名兒童，以及7,379名沒有受撫養人的單身成人。
對成人群體的細分揭示出一個顯著的模式。
男性占了58%以上，而25至44歲的人構成最大的族群，占超過51%。
一半擁有愛爾蘭國籍，31.4%是歐洲經濟區以外國家的公民，其餘18.6%來自歐洲經濟區或英國。
都柏林仍是這場危機的震央。

倡議團體對此感到沮喪。

都柏林西蒙社區表達深切關注，指出已連續第二個月有超過5,000名成年女性住在緊急安置住所，並提醒外界注意人數年增4.5%，呼籲政府介入。
此外，官方統計只呈現了部分情況。

paragraphs: Recently published government data indicate that homelessness in Ireland has continued its upward trajectory. The September figures, released by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage on Friday evening, had been expected on 30 October; however, their publication was deferred as a consequence of industrial action.

According to the statistics, 18,065 individuals were accommodated in emergency facilities in September, representing an increase of 180 on the previous month. This total comprised 5,897 children in 2,821 families and 7,379 single adults without dependent children.

The demographic composition of the adult population is equally significant. Men constituted more than 58% of adults, and individuals aged between 25 and 44 formed the predominant age group, at over 51%. In terms of nationality, half were Irish citizens, whereas 31.4% originated from outside the European Economic Area and 18.6% from the EEA or the UK.

Geographically, the problem is disproportionately concentrated in Dublin. In the week of 21 to 27 September alone, in excess of 8,300 adults utilised local-authority emergency accommodation in the capital, of whom 4,940 were single adults.

Unsurprisingly, the response from the voluntary sector was unequivocal. Ber Grogan, executive director of Simon Communities of Ireland, characterised the figures as "astoundingly depressing", observing that 47 more children were in emergency accommodation than in the preceding month. Similarly, Dublin Simon Community expressed deep concern that the number of adult women in emergency accommodation had exceeded 5,000 for a second consecutive month, noting a 4.5% year-on-year rise and calling on the Government to take decisive action.

Crucially, these figures are not exhaustive. They exclude people sleeping rough, those couch-surfing, individuals in domestic violence refuges and residents of direct provision who are unable to secure housing. Consequently, the true scale of homelessness is likely to be substantially greater than the official data suggest.

根據統計，九月有18,065人被安置在緊急住宿設施中，比前一個月增加180人。
這個總數包括2,821個家庭中的5,897名兒童，以及7,379名沒有受撫養子女的單身成人。
成人群體的人口組成同樣值得注意。
男性占成人的58%以上，而25至44歲的人構成主要年齡層，占超過51%。
在國籍方面，一半是愛爾蘭公民，而31.4%來自歐洲經濟區以外，18.6%來自歐洲經濟區或英國。
從地理上看，這個問題不成比例地集中在都柏林。
光是在9月21日至27日那一週，首都就有超過8,300名成人使用地方政府的緊急安置住所，其中4,940人為單身成人。
不出所料，志願部門的反應十分明確。
愛爾蘭西蒙社區執行董事伯．格羅根形容這些數字「令人極度沮喪」，並指出住在緊急安置住所的兒童比前一個月多了47名。
同樣地，都柏林西蒙社區對住在緊急安置住所的成年女性連續第二個月超過5,000人深表關切，指出人數年增4.5%，並呼籲政府採取果斷行動。
關鍵在於，這些數字並不完整。

因此，無家可歸的真實規模很可能遠大於官方數據所顯示的。
